Variants.Content: House Hotir lives within the sharply divided order of upper and lower Norvos. Cliffside stone stairs separate the highborn from the riverside laborers in space, yet the three great bells make everyone hear the same religious authority. House Hotir can accumulate wealth and marriage alliances, yet can hardly step openly beyond the boundaries drawn by the bearded priests. Norvos is divided into the upper city on the cliff and the lower city by the river. Giant bells, stone steps and axe-bearing monks jointly maintain the theocratic order dominated by bearded monks. Caravans, carpets, armor, and inland roads brought wealth, but noble families still had to respect religious judgment.
Entry Hotir Wealth can buy guards and mansions, but it is difficult to openly disobey those who have masters of divine law and armed monks.
Entry Hotir The upper-city banquets were far away from them, but every religious decision fell down the stone steps to the market-place.

Entry Hotir House Hotir is a house of Norvos whose standing rests on trade routes, urban holdings, kinship, and obedience to the theocracy of the bearded priests. The family crest is just a facade, the real weight of the family is whether they can protect their fiefdom, honor their engagements, and rally people in times of crisis.
